name: composite
summary: Ops assembled from the primitives rather than from a kernel.
extended:
118 functions defined in `lucid/_ops/composite/` — the aliases (`absolute`, `arctan2`, ...), the fused arithmetic helpers (`addmm`, `addcdiv`, ...), and the statistical and linear-algebra conveniences.

They carry no kernel and no backward of their own: gradients fall out of the primitives they are written in.  That makes them cheap to add and correct by construction, at the cost of materialising the intermediates a fused kernel would not.

members.name: equal
members.summary: Predicate: do two tensors have the same shape and the same elements?
members.extended:
One Python `bool` for the whole pair, unlike the element-wise
`lucid.eq`.  The shapes must match exactly — no broadcasting —
and the elements are compared at the pair's promoted dtype, so an
integer tensor equals the float tensor holding the same values.

returns.description:
`True` iff `input.shape == other.shape` and every element pair
compares equal.  `NaN` equals nothing, itself included, and
`-0.0` equals `0.0`.  Two empty tensors of one shape are equal.

raises.description: If either argument is not a `Tensor`.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> lucid.equal(lucid.tensor([1, 2]), lucid.tensor([1.0, 2.0]))
True
>>> lucid.equal(lucid.tensor([1, 2]), lucid.tensor([[1, 2]]))
False
notes: Reading the answer synchronises any pending Metal work on the pair.
